title: api: standardize rate-limit semantics and idempotency for streaming & tool calls (OpenAI-compat)
author: Ethan Zhao
description: Motivation: customers observed inconsistent rate-limit semantics and confusing error codes across our OpenAI-compat endpoints for streaming, tool/function calls, and structured output. This caused incorrect client retry behavior and surfaced as production incidents when autoscaling storms and duplicate streaming sessions occurred. This PR unifies server behavior for rate limiting and transient errors, enforces idempotency handling for streaming/tool-call entrypoints, and updates the OpenAI compatibility layer so clients receive predictable, documented errors. Changes include: 1) Standardize 429 and 503 semantics and always emit Retry-After in seconds when appropriate; 2) Enforce idempotency-key dedup for streaming endpoints and return 409 for conflicting sessions or 200 + cached session resume where appropriate; 3) Map internal transient errors to OpenAI-compat codes with consistent error.type and error.code fields; 4) Add defensive server-side guards to prevent double-accept of a single idempotency key across worker restarts; 5) Docs and SDK notes for migration and expected client behavior. Checklist: - [x] Implement server-side idempotency registry and streaming session state machine - [x] Standardize Retry-After header and retryable error mapping - [x] Update openai_compat response mapper and tests - [x] Add integration tests that simulate concurrent duplicate requests and autoscaling failover - [x] Update docs/openai-compat/rate-limits.md and release notes - [x] Run perf canary to validate no regression on steady-state latency (results attached) Breaking change: none for most users, but SDKs that relied on inconsistent error codes should work better after update. Related: ENG-4521 (rate-limit follow-ups), ENG-4580 (streaming stability), SUP-1234 (customer incident).

review_comments: Priya Menon: The mapping from our internal TEMP_UNAVAILABLE to openai's 503 looks good — can you confirm we include Retry-After in seconds in both header and response body?
Ethan Zhao: Yes — we emit Retry-After header in seconds and include retry_after_seconds in the OpenAI-compat error object for clients that inspect body instead of headers.

Marco Rivera: I hit a failing integration test locally for duplicate session detection — looks like a race when worker A commits then crashes before registry persistence. Can we make persistence atomic?
Ethan Zhao: Good catch — added a durable write-ahead log step and a short mutex window; updated tests to inject worker restart and validated recovery.
Aisha Patel: Docs LGTM. One suggestion: add small code snippet for SDKs showing expected 409 handling and resume flow.
Ethan Zhao: Added example snippet to docs and a Python SDK note in sdk/python/openai_compat_client.py.
Priya Menon: CI initially failed due to flaky test timing; after rerun all checks passed. Approving.
Marco Rivera: Approving after confirming canary shows <1% p99 latency regression.
release_notes: • Standardized rate-limit semantics and Retry-After behavior for OpenAI-compat APIs; clients should respect Retry-After header in seconds. • Streaming and tool/function-call endpoints now enforce idempotency keys to avoid duplicate sessions; conflicting duplicate requests return 409 or resume cached session where applicable. • Error responses are now consistent (structured error.type and error.code) across OpenAI-compat layer. • No breaking changes expected; SDKs may be updated to handle 409/resume flow more cleanly.
